definition: Finite people, actions, contexts and goods have explicit factual relations: actor, target, nonconsent, deliberate killing, victim innocence and nonthreat, offender indifference, benefit, absence of punishment, feasibility, recognition and realization of promise keeping and harm prevention. Separately supplied verdicts contain forbidden and categorical-reason-against predicates; ideal-successor frames define the two compared duties.
note: These analyst assignments distinguish actual case properties from normative predicates; lack of prohibition is not permission. One action realizes only the promise good and one realizes only the serious-harm-prevention good. Neither actual feasibility nor actual priority is established. The named types are finite controls rather than complete historical theories.
